html:
The Constitution of Ecuador of 2008 was the first in the world to give rights to nature itself. Voters approved it in a referendum on 28 September 2008.

It was drafted by an assembly in Montecristi called by President Rafael Correa. It named Ecuador a plurinational state, made Kichwa and Shuar official languages of intercultural relations, and set as a goal sumak kawsay, a Kichwa idea of living well in balance with the community and the earth. Nature, or Pachamama, was given the right to exist and to be restored, which any person can defend in court.

Courts have since used these rights to stop mining and protect rivers and forests. The idea spread to Bolivia and to laws elsewhere. It drew on the demands of the Indigenous movement.
sum: The Constitution of Ecuador of 2008 was the first in the world to give rights to nature itself. Voters approved it in a referendum on 28 September 2008.
